sources.cite: CDC. Implementation of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) Use in Nursing Homes to Prevent Spread of Multidrug-resistant Organisms (MDROs) (last reviewed 2024-04-02)
sources.note: Relayed from the LPNVN case ltc-pressure-injury-infection, not re-read for this band; its note: Read 2026-11-11 (primary web page). Enhanced Barrier Precautions apply to residents with 'Wounds and/or indwelling medical devices' regardless of MDRO status; gown and gloves for high-contact care, which lists 'Wound care: any skin opening requiring a dressing'.

sources.cite: NPIAP. Pressure Injury Stages (staging poster, September 2016)
sources.note: Relayed from the LPNVN case ltc-pressure-injury-infection, not re-read for this band; its note: Read 2026-11-11 (primary poster, VUMC copy). Stage 3: full-thickness skin loss, adipose may be visible, slough and/or eschar may be visible, undermining and tunneling may occur; fascia, muscle, tendon, ligament, cartilage or bone are not exposed.

sources.cite: Singer M, et al. The Third International Consensus Definitions for Sepsis and Septic Shock (Sepsis-3). JAMA 2016;315(8):801-810
sources.note: Relayed from the LPNVN case ltc-pressure-injury-infection, not re-read for this band; its note: Read 2026-11-11 (primary PDF, BUMC copy). qSOFA: respiratory rate 22/min or greater, altered mentation, systolic BP 100 mmHg or less; two or more in an adult with suspected infection flags a higher risk of poor outcomes; designed for out-of-hospital, ED and ward settings; not meeting it should not delay work-up.
